metadata.file_name: 87. Kara. (2025). Exploring Test-Taking Disengagement in the Context of PISA 2022: Evidence from Process Data.pdf
metadata.title: Exploring Test-Taking Disengagement in the Context of PISA 2022: Evidence from Process Data
metadata.venue: International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 process data and self-reported effort items for the Turkish sample, then constructs person-level indicators (response time, number of actions, and response-time-effort indices) and applies Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) to classify students into engagement profiles. The manuscript reports listwise deletion for missing process indicators, but it does not describe the use of PISA sampling weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the LPA or descriptive/correlation analyses. Because LPA and standard correlation procedures are not explicitly documented as weight-aware here, the weighting approach is unclear from the text; analysts should consult the PISA technical documentation and the authors’ data-analysis code (if available) to confirm whether complex survey design weights were applied. For replication, weighting should follow PISA’s complex sampling design guidance (student sampling weights for point estimates; replicate weights for variance estimation) and should be applied consistently across profile estimation and achievement comparisons.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is restricted to the Turkish PISA 2022 students who completed the mathematics computer-based assessment and for whom response time (RT) and number of actions (NA) could be computed; missing values on these process indicators were excluded using listwise deletion. This cleaning step reduced the sample from 7250 to 6560 students. The study focuses on mathematics performance and uses the PISA effort thermometer self-reported effort item (SRE) together with process-based indicators to estimate engagement profiles.

main_findings.performance_metrics: LPA fit: optimal 3-profile solution; AIC 51750.54, BIC 51845.58, aBIC 51801.09; entropy 0.883; LMR test p < .05. Profile sizes: Profile 1 (Moderately-Engaged) 5431; Profile 2 (Highly-Engaged) 472; Profile 3 (Disengaged) 657. Profile differences: ANOVA p < .05; Tukey post-hoc p < .05 for RT, NA, and SRE across all profiles. Additional analysis (Mathematics achievement differences across engagement profiles): Profile-specific mean mathematics achievement: Profile 2 (Highly-Engaged) 536.453; Profile 3 (Disengaged) 421.74; Profile 1 (Moderately-Engaged) 452.689. Differences reported as statistically significant for each group (exact test statistic not provided).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics (Turkey) process data, the study leveraged response time (RT), number of actions (NA), and self-reported effort (SRE) to classify students into engagement profiles, finding that a three-profile structure best captured engagement heterogeneity (Moderately-Engaged, Highly-Engaged, Disengaged). This indicates that disengagement is not uniform but forms a distinct subgroup that can be identified from combined behavioral and self-report indicators, supporting assessment practices that flag low-effort responding when interpreting achievement results.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 mathematics process data for Turkey, focusing on three engagement indicators: response time (RT), number of actions (NA), and self-reported effort (SRE) from the PISA effort thermometer. After listwise deletion of missing process indicators, the analytic sample contains 6560 students. The authors first show that engagement distributions vary substantially by thresholding approach (RTE_5sec, RTE_10p, and NA_10p), and that NA correlates most strongly with mathematics achievement (r = .43), while SRE shows the weakest association (r = .02). Using latent profile analysis, they select a three-profile solution (entropy = 0.883) and find that the Disengaged profile (10.01%) has the lowest mean mathematics achievement (421.74) compared with the Moderately-Engaged (452.689) and Highly-Engaged (536.453) profiles. A key limitation is that the manuscript does not report survey-weight handling for PISA’s complex design, and the profile-based approach is person-centered rather than a predictive ML model.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models; instead, it uses Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) to uncover latent engagement subgroups and then compares mathematics achievement across profiles. Therefore, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty (no supervised learner is reported), and the study is classified as exploratory rather than predictive.
